workflows.title: Check a suspicious file
workflows.summary: Start with an existing hash report, then choose static or behavioral analysis for the question that remains.
steps: Calculate the file hash locally and search for an existing report before sending file bytes to a service.
Compare detection names, report age, signer and behavior; choose a sandbox when you need to understand execution.
Record the exact hash and findings, then use the malware guide to verify the affected endpoint and choose cleanup or rebuild.

workflows.title: Inspect a suspicious link
workflows.summary: Combine reputation with redirects and page behavior without opening the destination on the customer’s workstation.
steps: Copy the destination as text and search existing reports; inspect the hostname before following a link.

For a new scan, choose a visibility mode suitable for the URL; use an existing report, hostname lookup or appropriate private workflow for a token-bearing link. Record any input redaction because it can change page behavior.
Compare redirects, page requests and reputation; follow the incident guide if someone entered credentials or downloaded a payload.

workflows.title: Investigate an IP or domain
workflows.summary: Use several dated sources to explain reputation, exposed services and ownership.
steps: Look up the exact indicator and record when each source last observed it.
Compare scanner noise, abuse reports, service banners and network ownership with the actual firewall evidence.
Confirm the current connection and scope before changing a block rule; shared hosting and old reports can change the interpretation.

workflows.title: Diagnose email and DNS
workflows.summary: Separate DNS, sender authentication and service availability before changing a mailbox.
steps: Check the domain’s MX and TXT records, the full delivery error and the provider’s service status.
Inspect SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment, and use message-header analysis or a non-sensitive test message when needed.
After one targeted correction, send and receive the same test and record the resulting authentication and delivery evidence.

workflows.title: Check website security
workflows.summary: Combine complementary configuration tests for a public site.
steps: Run a TLS and certificate check against the exact public hostname you maintain.
Inspect security headers and internet configuration separately; map each finding to its server or application owner.
Apply a targeted change, rerun the matching check, and verify sign-in, embeds and the normal user journey still work.

workflows.title: Find latency or an outage
workflows.summary: Separate bandwidth, latency under load, local faults and regional reachability.
steps: Measure from one wired device and record idle latency, loaded latency, loss and the time of the symptom.
Compare a second device or path, then use external vantage points and provider status to locate the failing boundary.
Retest the original call, stream or business application after the change; a download-speed result alone is not the completion test.

workflows.title: Prioritize a vulnerability
workflows.summary: Combine affected-version evidence, known exploitation and likely exploitation without treating them as the same metric.
steps: Match the advisory to the installed product and exact version; check vendor remediation and prerequisites.
Check known exploitation and current probability alongside severity and actual exposure.
Apply the applicable vendor fix in a recovery-ready window, then verify the version and the service’s original workload.

workflows.title: Improve a slow website
workflows.summary: Turn performance and accessibility reports into changes with a visible user result.
steps: Test the exact affected page and device conditions; distinguish lab runs from available real-user measurements.
Trace the slow resource or failed interaction, make one targeted change and preserve readable content and keyboard access.
Repeat the same test conditions and the actual user task; supplement automated accessibility findings with manual checks.

workflows.title: Decode and document evidence
workflows.summary: Use purpose-specific browser tools to understand a sample of evidence and leave a clear handoff.
steps: Choose the operation for the question: decode a value, match a pattern, diagram a dependency or reproduce an API request.
Check whether that operation is local, synchronized, proxied or sent to a remote service before supplying case data.
Keep the original evidence and save the recipe, request or editable diagram plus the observed result.

workflows.title: Explain a blocked website
workflows.summary: Match the blocked URL to the security product that made the decision, then separate a policy decision from a classification error.
steps: Capture the exact public hostname, block time, security product and category from the block page or gateway log.
Look up the URL in the matching vendor portal and compare its category with the intended policy; request a category correction when the evidence supports it.
Retest the original website from the affected device after the approved category or policy change, and confirm protection for unrelated traffic remains effective.

workflows.title: Investigate a Windows binary or driver
workflows.summary: Use exact-file identity and observed behavior to interpret a signed-process or kernel-driver alert.
steps: Preserve the exact file hash, signer, full path, command line, parent process and alert time from the affected endpoint.
Compare driver hashes with LOLDrivers or signed-binary behavior with LOLBAS, then corroborate with the dated file report and local telemetry.
Choose a targeted vendor fix, containment step or defensive control based on the evidence, and verify the original workload and security state after the change.

workflows.title: Check a cloud service outage
workflows.summary: Match the provider, component, region and incident time before changing a customer’s endpoint configuration.
steps: Identify the failing provider, component and region, and compare the symptom time with the official incident timeline.
If public status does not explain the issue, check the authorized tenant/account health view and reproduce from a second path or device.
Record the matching incident or failed diagnostic boundary, then retest the original customer task after recovery.

workflows.title: Fix a certificate renewal failure
workflows.summary: Separate ACME issuance, deployed certificate and server TLS configuration before applying a repair.
steps: Read the ACME client failure and test the exact hostname with its actual HTTP-01, DNS-01 or TLS-ALPN-01 validation method.
Repair the first matching DNS, CAA, routing or challenge-path fault, then rerun the actual renewal and verify the certificate deployed to every intended endpoint.
Check the live TLS result and the real client workflow; use a configuration generator only with the correct server versions and compatibility requirements.
